title: Deep catastrophic-risk-aware reinforcement learning
summary: Estimating extreme risk in reinforcement learning becomes increasingly difficult as the confidence level increases, since only a small number of observations contribute to empirical estimates of Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR). In this paper, we extend an Extreme Value Theory (EVT) approach for CVaR optimization to high-dimensional neural-network policies. Using a peaks-over-threshold representation and method-of-moments estimation, we obtain a differentiable tail-risk objective and show that, conditional on the selected threshold, its finite-sample gradient can be computed directly through automatic differentiation. We first validate the approach in a controlled experiment with a known optimal solution and then investigate its performance in a deep-hedging problem with rare extreme market movements. Our results show similar hedging behavior for EVT- and empirical-CVaR-trained policies under normal conditions, while EVT-trained policies exhibit lower hedging losses under the extreme-scenario evaluation across the training sample sizes considered. These results suggest that EVT can provide a practical alternative for training neural policies when the observations relevant to extreme risk are scarce.
core_methodology: Extends Extreme Value Theory (EVT) approach for Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) optimization to high-dimensional neural-network policies using a peaks-over-threshold representation and method-of-moments estimation, resulting in a differentiable tail-risk objective.
data_sources: Financial market data for deep-hedging problem with rare extreme market movements.
alpha_potential: The methodology allows for better estimation and optimization of extreme risks in trading strategies, particularly valuable for managing tail risks in portfolios and hedging strategies, especially during rare market extremes where traditional methods may fail.
title_cn: 深度灾难风险感知的强化学习
summary_cn: 该研究通过极值理论(EVT)扩展了条件风险价值(CVaR)优化方法，适用于高维神经网络策略。在极端市场条件下，基于EVT训练的策略展现出比传统CVaR方法更优的对冲表现，对于量化投资中的尾部风险管理具有直接应用价值。

title: Universal Online Convex Optimization With Delayed Feedback
summary: We study universal online convex optimization with delayed feedback. We develop a single algorithm that simultaneously adapts to general convex, strongly convex, and exp-concave losses without prior knowledge of the curvature class or parameters. Our regret bounds match the best known dependence on the time horizon $T$ and delays up to doubly logarithmic factors: roughly $\sqrt{T + d_{\mathrm{tot}}}$ for convex losses and $\sigma_{\max}\log T$ rates with curved losses, where $d_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total cumulative delay and $\sigma_{\max}$ is the maximum number of simultaneously missing observations. Our main technical contribution is a delayed meta-learner with a second-order excess-loss guarantee, which enables curvature-adaptive aggregation of delayed base learners. In addition, our new exp-concave base learner yields a sharper regret bound which improves the state-of-the-art delay dependence by replacing the maximum delay with the potentially much smaller $\sigma_{\max}$, while retaining the complementary $\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{tot}}}$ dependence.
core_methodology: Universal online convex optimization algorithm that adapts to different loss curvature (convex, strongly convex, exp-concave) without prior knowledge of curvature parameters, using delayed feedback aggregation with second-order excess-loss guarantees
data_sources: General theoretical framework applicable to any time-series market data (prices, fundamentals, alternative data) with delayed feedback scenarios
alpha_potential: Potentially significant for: 1) Delayed information arbitrage strategies, 2) Optimal execution with delayed market impact feedback, 3) Portfolio optimization under information delays. The curvature adaptation could capture various market regimes while handling data latency inherent in trading systems
title_cn: 具有延迟反馈的通用在线凸优化
summary_cn: 该研究提出的通用延迟反馈在线凸优化算法，可自动适应市场不同波动形态（凸、强凸、指数凹），无需预设参数。其随时间延迟优化的特性特别适合高频交易中的信息延迟场景和处理不同市场状态下的资产组合优化问题，为延迟套利和最优执行策略提供理论基础。

title: LOB-Impact Benchmark: Emergent Market Impact in Generative Limit Order Book Models
summary: Realistic market impact is essential for generative limit order book (LOB) models to serve as world models for trading agents. If a simulator misprices this mechanism, agents learn policies that are optimal in the simulator but wrong in the real market. Existing metrics assess generated streams purely through distributional comparison with historical data, leaving counterfactual response to an agent's own orders largely unexplored. Here, we show that market impact emerges naturally in neural LOB generators trained solely for next-token prediction. We inject execution-style metaorders into the generated message flow of five autoregressive models across five NASDAQ stocks and measure the response using estimators from the empirical impact literature, validated on baselines whose physics is known in advance. Our benchmark evaluates any message-level generator in three phases: free generation (reading order-flow persistence against price diffusivity); metaorder injection (yielding the impact law's exponent and amplitude); and a post-execution window (measuring relaxation). In addition, comparing each visible injection to a blind, simulator-only control isolates the model's learned response from standard book mechanics. For every model on every stock, we measure how the impact responds as a function of cumulative metaorder participation. Interestingly, we observe emergent impact in generative models of market data, with exponents in the range of 0.63 to 1.21, slightly above the traditional 0.5 of the square-root law of impact. In the family of models tested, we are so far unable to observe impact decay during relaxation. We tentatively attribute this to the still-short context windows of the models. We release the benchmark as open source to validate future generative models for market data.
core_methodology: The paper evaluates neural LOB generators trained for next-token prediction by measuring emergent market impact through execution-style metaorder injections and comparing responses using empirical impact estimators. The benchmark includes three phases: free generation, metaorder injection, and post-execution relaxation measurement.
data_sources: Five NASDAQ stocks are used to validate the methodology, with execution-style metaorders injected into the generated message flow of five autoregressive models.
alpha_potential: The paper demonstrates that market impact emerges naturally in generative LOB models, with impact exponents ranging from 0.63 to 1.21, slightly above the traditional square-root law of impact. This has significant implications for training trading agents that can better simulate real-market conditions and optimize execution strategies.
title_cn: LOB-Impact Benchmark: 生成限价订单簿模型中的涌现市场影响
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基准测试方法，用于评估生成限价订单簿模型中的市场影响效应。通过注入模拟订单并测量响应，论文显示神经LOB模型通过学习自然涌现出市场影响效应，其指数范围略高于传统的平方根定律。这对于训练更真实的交易代理和执行策略优化具有重要价值。

title: Covariance-Aware Transformers for Quadratic Programming and Decision Making
summary: We explore the use of transformers for solving quadratic programs and how this capability benefits decision-making problems that involve covariance matrices. We first show that the linear attention mechanism can provably solve unconstrained QPs by tokenizing the matrix variables (e.g.~$A$ of the objective $\frac{1}{2}x^\top Ax+b^\top x$) row-by-row and emulating gradient descent iterations. Furthermore, by incorporating MLPs, a transformer block can solve (i) $\ell_1$-penalized QPs by emulating iterative soft-thresholding and (ii) $\ell_1$-constrained QPs when equipped with an additional feedback loop. Our theory motivates us to introduce Time2Decide: a generic method that enhances a time series foundation model (TSFM) by explicitly feeding the covariance matrix between the variates. We empirically find that Time2Decide uniformly outperforms the base TSFM model for the classical portfolio optimization problem that admits an $\ell_1$-constrained QP formulation. Remarkably, Time2Decide also outperforms the classical "Predict-then-Optimize (PtO)" procedure, where we first forecast the returns and then explicitly solve a constrained QP, in suitable settings. Our results demonstrate that transformers benefit from explicit use of second-order statistics, and this can enable them to effectively solve complex decision-making problems, like portfolio construction, in one forward pass.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a transformer-based method called Time2Decide that solves quadratic programs (QPs) using linear attention mechanisms and MLPs. It specifically addresses QPs with covariance matrices, which are common in portfolio optimization problems. The method outperforms traditional 'Predict-then-Optimize' approaches by incorporating second-order statistics directly into the transformer architecture.
data_sources: Implies use of financial time series data with covariance matrices, typical in portfolio optimization contexts (e.g., stock returns, volatility data).
alpha_potential: High potential for improving portfolio optimization strategies by directly incorporating covariance-aware transformers, potentially leading to better risk-adjusted returns and more efficient asset allocation decisions.
title_cn: 用于二次规划和决策的协方差感知Transformer
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种基于Transformer的方法Time2Decide，通过线性注意力和MLP直接求解包含协方差矩阵的二次规划问题。在投资组合优化中，该方法优于传统的'预测后优化'流程，能在单次前向传播中有效解决复杂决策问题，为量化投资提供了新工具。

title: Market Regime-Based Multi-Asset Portfolio Optimization Using Nested Clustered Optimization for Tactical Asset Allocation
summary: We propose a regime-aware tactical asset allocation (TAA) framework integrating market regime detection with Nested Clustered Optimization (NCO) for multi-asset portfolio construction. The central hypothesis is that incorporating market regime information into the NCO pipeline, specifically at the stages of covariance estimation, hierarchical clustering, and weight optimization, yields portfolios with improved risk-adjusted performance and reduced downside risk relative to regime-agnostic baselines. Market regimes (Bullish, Sideways/Neutral, Bearish) are detected using a Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM) fitted exclusively on information available up to each decision point, thereby preventing look-ahead bias. Regime-conditional covariance matrices and clustering structures parameterize NCO at each rebalancing event. An adaptive rebalancing rule, triggered by regime transitions or material changes in optimal weights, replaces fixed-calendar rebalancing. The framework is evaluated on a heterogeneous monthly multi-asset universe comprising Indonesian government bonds (SBN), the LQ45 equity index, gold (IDR-denominated), foreign exchange (CNY/IDR), and Bitcoin/IDR (BTC). Out-of-sample performance is assessed via rolling walk-forward backtesting. Benchmarks include equal-weight (1/N), buy-and-hold, standard NCO without regime awareness, minimum variance, hierarchical risk parity (HRP), and a rule-based regime strategy. Performance metrics include cumulative return, annualized Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, maximum drawdown, Calmar ratio, turnover, and net-of-cost returns. Statistical significance is assessed using the Jobson-Korkie test. The empirical analysis indicates that the proposed regime-aware TAA framework successfully limits tail risk, achieving a maximum drawdown of 4.44% and demonstrating the utility of HMM-based regime detection in multi-asset risk management.
core_methodology: The paper presents a regime-aware tactical asset allocation framework that integrates Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for market regime detection with Nested Clustered Optimization (NCO) for portfolio construction. The methodology includes regime-conditional covariance matrices, hierarchical clustering, and adaptive rebalancing triggered by regime transitions.
data_sources: The framework is evaluated on a heterogeneous monthly multi-asset universe comprising Indonesian government bonds (SBN), the LQ45 equity index, gold (IDR-denominated), foreign exchange (CNY/IDR), and Bitcoin/IDR (BTC).
alpha_potential: The model exploits market regime shifts which are persistent inefficiencies that can be captured through statistical modelling. The combination of regime-aware clustering and optimization improves risk-adjusted returns and reduces tail risk, which is a key component of sustainable alpha generation.
title_cn: 基于市场状态的多资产组合优化：利用嵌套聚类优化进行战术资产配置
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种结合市场状态检测与嵌套聚类优化(NCO)的战术资产配置框架。使用高斯隐马尔可夫模型(HMM)实时识别市场状态(牛市/盘整/熊市)，并将状态信息融入协方差估计、层次聚类和权重优化全过程。在印尼多资产组合(国债、股票、黄金、外汇、比特币)的实证中，该框架显著降低尾部风险(最大回撤4.44%)，展示出状态感知策略在风险调整收益上的优势。

title: Navalia: Advancing Cowork Agents through Verifiable Task Synthesis and Long-Horizon Post-Training
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are evolving from conversational assistants into Cowork Agents capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and complex task execution. Financial analysis requires these agents to integrate cross-document evidence and perform multistep numerical reasoning, but expert task authoring is costly, while direct LLM synthesis struggles to produce challenging tasks with reliable answers. We introduce Navalia, a framework for Cowork Agents that combines verifiable task synthesis with long-horizon post-training. Using corporate financial reports as its data source, Navalia semantically selects supporting evidence from complete fact sets and constructs executable computation chains to generate analytical tasks with traceable evidence and actual data dependencies between steps. We further use independent LLM review and programmatic checks to verify evidence consistency and answer correctness. The verified tasks are then used for trajectory collection, cold-start supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL) to improve long-horizon task execution. Navalia, initialized from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, achieves consistent gains over the base model across all five benchmarks: OfficeQA Pro, FinSearchComp, Finance Agent Benchmark, APEX-Agents-AA, and Workspace-Bench-Lite. These results demonstrate that Navalia improves evidence integration, tool use, and long-horizon task execution capabilities and generalizes to broader Cowork settings, including general office tasks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Navalia, a framework combining verifiable task synthesis and long-horizon post-training to enhance LLM agents' capabilities in financial analysis. The methodology involves semantic selection of supporting evidence from financial reports, construction of executable computation chains, and verification through independent LLM review and programmatic checks. The framework utilizes cold-start supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) to improve long-horizon task execution.
data_sources: Corporate financial reports are used as the primary data source for task synthesis and evidence integration.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to integrate cross-document evidence and perform multistep numerical reasoning could uncover hidden patterns or inefficiencies in financial data, potentially leading to actionable trading signals or improved financial analysis.
title_cn: Navalia：通过可验证的任务合成和长周期后训练推进协作代理
summary_cn: Navalia框架通过结合可验证的任务合成和长周期后训练，提升LLM代理在金融分析中的能力。该框架利用公司财务报告作为数据源，构建可执行的计算链，并通过独立LLM审核和程序化检查验证结果的准确性。这一方法有望在金融数据分析中发现潜在的市场信号，为量化交易提供新的分析工具。

title: ORBIT: Autoregressive Time Series Generation via Next Frequency-Band Prediction
summary: Deep generative models provide an effective modern solution to alleviating the problem of data scarcity by synthesizing realistic time series. However, despite the considerable progress achieved by existing deep time series generators, two key challenges remain: (1) learning hierarchical representations for heterogeneous temporal patterns; and (2) coordinating the generation process of heterogeneous temporal dynamics. To address these key bottlenecks, in this work, we propose ORBIT, a unified deep generative framework for time series. Specifically, we develop two key components: the Frequency-Hierarchical VQ-VAE (FH-VQ-VAE) and the Frequency-Band Autoregressive Transformer (FBAR). The former learns hierarchical representations by decomposing latent temporal representations into different frequency bands and applying residual quantization with increasing token budgets. The latter establishes a novel low-to-high frequency autoregressive direction, yielding a time series generation process that first constructs global temporal structures and then incrementally incorporates fine-grained temporal details. These compact designs not only disentangle heterogeneous temporal patterns for more effective representation learning but also mitigate potential interference among different temporal dynamics during generation. Extensive experiments on multiple challenging real-world benchmarks demonstrate that ORBIT achieves state-of-the-art overall performance while exhibiting superior inference efficiency compared with advanced baselines.
core_methodology: Frequency-Hierarchical VQ-VAE (FH-VQ-VAE) for hierarchical representation learning and Frequency-Band Autoregressive Transformer (FBAR) for low-to-high frequency autoregressive time series generation
data_sources: Real-world benchmarks (specific datasets not mentioned but likely includes diverse time series data relevant to financial markets)
alpha_potential: Potential for generating synthetic financial time series data for backtesting, stress testing, and augmenting training datasets for trading models. The hierarchical frequency approach may help capture multi-scale market patterns better than traditional methods.
title_cn: 基于下一频段预测的自回归时间序列生成模型ORBIT
summary_cn: ORBIT提出了一种高效的时间序列生成框架，通过频域层级表征学习与由低频至高频的自回归生成过程，可合成高保真金融时序数据。该系统在构建全局市场结构后逐步添加细节的特性，使其在交易策略回测与风险压力测试的数据增强方面具有显著应用价值。

title: Cross-Lingual Reusability of LLM Pipelines: Financial Extraction, Multilingual Reasoning, and Semantic Screening
summary: Financial institutions increasingly deploy large language models (LLMs) in multilingual markets, raising a practical question: can pipelines developed and validated in English be reused across languages, or must they be rebuilt per locale? We test cross-lingual reusability along three dimensions--accuracy, reasoning-effort transfer, and behavioural stability--through three complementary tasks. Task 1 (cheque extraction) and Task 2 (Mintaka QA with pinned evidence across nine languages and nine model-effort configurations) test whether accuracy and effort settings transfer; Task 3 (FinanceBench pilot, 50 items over SEC 10-K filings in four languages) validates whether these patterns generalise to financial content. Accuracy reusability is broadly confirmed: Gemini 3.5 Flash achieves 95.2-97.6% extraction accuracy across prompt languages, and FinanceBench per-language means span 5.8pp (77.1-82.9%), though the language-difficulty ranking reverses between domains (Hindi is worst on Mintaka, best on FinanceBench at 82.9%). Effort reusability is domain-dependent: higher reasoning effort yields marginal gains on general-knowledge QA but up to 8pp on financial content, and effort configurations that help in English help proportionally in other languages. Behavioural reusability holds: citation-set overlap with English averages 77-79% Jaccard, with no single language consistently worse. Together, these results support qualified reuse of English-built pipelines, but per-domain, per-language validation remains necessary--neither semantic similarity nor self-reported confidence reliably predicts cross-lingual accuracy.
core_methodology: Cross-lingual evaluation of LLM pipelines in financial tasks, testing accuracy, reasoning-effort transfer, and behavioral stability across multiple languages and domains.
data_sources: Multilingual financial documents (cheques), QA datasets (Mintaka), SEC 10-K filings (FinanceBench) across nine languages.
alpha_potential: Enables scalable deployment of financial NLP pipelines in global markets with reduced localization costs, particularly valuable for cross-border financial document processing and multilingual sentiment analysis.
title_cn: LLM管道的跨语言复用性：财务信息抽取、多语言推理与语义筛选
summary_cn: 本研究验证了英语训练的LLM管道在财务领域跨语言复用的可行性（准确率95.2-97.6%），通过支票信息抽取、双语QA和SEC文件处理三个任务发现：1) 准确率可跨语言迁移但需按语言验证；2) 推理效率配置在金融领域增益显著(8pp)；3) 行为一致性高（Jaccard 77-79%）。为量化交易中多语言财务文本处理提供了高效解决方案。

title: Meta-iLaD: Identifiable Latent Dynamics via Meta-Learning of Dynamics Environments
summary: Learning latent dynamics is central to assessing the current states and forecasting the future trajectories of high-dimensional time series. For locally-stationary latent dynamics $\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{z}_{<t}; \mathbf{c})$ with latent dynamics state $\mathbf{z}_t$ and environment variable $\mathbf{c}$, prior identifiability results have largely focused on $\mathbf{z}_t$ when conditioned on predefined label $u$ of dynamics environments. This leaves two limitations: reliance on predefined labels that hinder generalization to unseen environments, and a limited understanding of the identifiability of $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathbf{c}$ which -- although offering important structural properties for the identifiability of $\mathbf{z}_t$ -- are learned jointly with $\mathbf{z}_t$. We address these limitations with Meta-iLaD, a novel identifiable latent dynamics framework attained by meta-learning across dynamics environments. Meta-iLaD introduces a novel conditional prior of $\mathbf{c}$, modeled as a feedforward meta-learner to rapidly extract $\mathbf{c}$ from few-shot examples. Meta-iLaD further establishes identifiability for $\mathbf{z}_t$, $\mathbf{c}$, and $\mathcal{F}$ simultaneously, for a general formulation of $\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{z}_{< t};\mathbf{c})$ without restricting the dimension of $\mathbf{c}$ or how it modulates $\mathcal{F}$. On synthetic and real data, we provide strong empirical evidence that 1) conditioning on few-shot examples enables generalization to out-of-distribution environments, and 2) identifiability for $\mathbf{c}$ and $\mathcal{F}$ is critical for accurate forecasting beyond reconstructing observed trajectories. Code is available at https://github.com/GoForIt-YYB/Meta-iLaD.
core_methodology: Meta-learning framework for identifiable latent dynamics (Meta-iLaD) that simultaneously learns latent states (z_t), environment variables (c), and dynamics functions (F) across non-stationary environments through few-shot adaptation
data_sources: Tested on both synthetic and real-world time series data (though unspecified if financial)
alpha_potential: Enables adaptive modeling of regime-switching markets and out-of-sample generalization - critical for forecasting under structural breaks. The identifiability of environment variables (c) could help detect latent market regimes.
title_cn: Meta-iLaD：通过动态环境元学习实现可识别的潜动态
summary_cn: 该论文提出通过元学习跨环境建立可识别的潜动态模型（z_t, c, F），无需预定义环境标签。对量化交易的实用价值在于：1) 少量样本适应新市场状态的能力，2) 可识别环境变量c可能用于检测未见的市场机制切换，3) 动态函数F的显式学习提升非平稳环境下的预测性能。

title: Training-Free Continual Learning for Multimodal Forecasting via Prompt Evolution
summary: Adapting a forecasting system to a changing world classically means retraining. We ask whether the task of continually learning regimes for time series forecasting can be represented by a piece of text: a guidance block, evolved by outcome-driven reflection and used in a frozen LLM forecaster's prompt. On a refreshed multimodal benchmark (weekly search indices, daily currencies, daily commodities, each window paired with web-retrieved news), we run GEPA-style prompt evolution under strict contamination control to prevent the data leakage common in timeseries benchmarks: the forecaster's knowledge cutoff predates every evaluated window. A 900-word evolved guidance carried by Llama-3.3-70B beats TimeSeries Foundation Models (TSFMs) on held-out data (GM MASE 0.776 vs. 0.898 for TabPFN-TS-3), transfers to more recent models without measurable loss, and costs dollars rather than GPU-days to update. We characterize the loop: out-of-loop gains concentrate in the first reflection, in-loop improvements overstate out-of-loop gains 2-3x unless an untouched monitor arbitrates, and error-only objectives silently suppress the text modality. We provide two extensions. First, compiling the guidance into executable code with a TSFM as a callable tool recovers most of the gain deterministically. Second, ablations show the advantage widens at short horizons and that removing the news text does not hurt the guided forecaster, consistent with the text's value being distilled into policy during learning. We argue that continual prompt evolution is a practical, training-free alternative to retraining for multimodal forecasting.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a training-free continual learning approach for multimodal forecasting using prompt evolution in frozen LLMs. It focuses on evolving a guidance block through outcome-driven reflection and uses this in the prompt of an LLM forecaster. The methodology includes GEPA-style prompt evolution with strict contamination control to avoid data leakage, and it also explores compiling the evolved guidance into executable code with a TSFM as a callable tool.
data_sources: The research uses a multimodal benchmark comprising weekly search indices, daily currencies, daily commodities, each paired with web-retrieved news. The data is carefully controlled to ensure the forecaster's knowledge cutoff predates every evaluated window.
alpha_potential: The approach demonstrates clear alpha potential by outperforming TimeSeries Foundation Models (TSFMs) on held-out data, with a GM MASE of 0.776 vs. 0.898 for TabPFN-TS-3. The method is cost-effective (dollars vs. GPU-days for updates) and shows transferability to more recent models without measurable loss. The distilled policy from news text into the guidance block suggests potential for capturing latent signals in financial news and market data.
title_cn: 通过提示进化实现无需训练的多模态预测持续学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种无需训练的持续学习方法，通过提示进化在冻结的大语言模型中进行多模态预测。该方法在多种金融时间序列数据上表现出色，优于传统时间序列基础模型，且成本低廉，具有实时更新潜力。特别适合金融新闻和市场数据的动态预测应用。

title: OptScientist: Automated Discovery of Optimization Laws
summary: Many scientific phenomena are best understood as outcomes of underlying optimization problems, yet automated scientific discovery has largely focused on recovering equations that describe observed input-output patterns. We introduce OptScientist, a novel automated framework for discovering compact symbolic optimization laws directly from data. OptScientist comprises (i) a model that infers symbolic optimization problems by first learning to represent data as an optimization problem and then extracting its symbolic form, and (ii) an LLM agentic system embedding the model in a discovery process that integrates theoretical priors from scientific literature, discovers candidate laws, abstracts their underlying mechanisms, and suggests new data to collect. We first evaluate OptScientist on OptFeynman, a novel benchmark of 99 physics-derived optimization problems, where OptScientist recovers ground-truth laws for over 80% of the problems and remains robust to noisy contextual information, while substantially outperforming machine-learning, symbolic, and LLM-based model-discovery baselines. On human risky choice and central-bank monetary policy, OptScientist discovers compact symbolic optimization laws that achieve held-out predictive performance competitive with leading baselines, while using few parameters and substantially fewer tokens than LLM baselines. Overall, OptScientist extends automated scientific discovery to uncovering optimization laws that generate observed phenomena, enabling automated theory building across the physical, biological, behavioral, and social sciences.
core_methodology: OptScientist combines symbolic optimization discovery with LLM agentic systems to infer compact optimization laws from data, integrating theoretical priors and suggesting new data collection. It includes learning to represent data as optimization problems and extracting their symbolic forms.
data_sources: Human risky choice data and central-bank monetary policy data, as well as physics-derived optimization problems for benchmarking.
alpha_potential: High potential for discovering compact optimization models that can predict financial behaviors or policy outcomes with fewer parameters and tokens compared to traditional LLM approaches, suggesting efficiency in modeling complex financial systems.
title_cn: OptScientist：优化定律的自动化发现
summary_cn: OptScientist通过结合符号优化和LLM代理系统，直接从数据中发现紧凑的优化定律，适用于金融行为和货币政策预测。其高效建模能力在金融预测领域展现出明显优势，尤其是在参数和计算资源使用上相比传统方法更为节省。

title: Dynamic Dual-Feedback Conformal Inference for Time Series Forecasting
summary: Quantifying uncertainty in time series forecasting is particularly demanding because sequential data exhibit temporal dependence and are prone to distributional changes. Conformal inference has emerged as a powerful uncertainty quantification approach through the construction of prediction sets. Recent advances have introduced online conformal methods that adaptively adjust prediction thresholds through feedback mechanisms. However, the existing feedback mechanism typically relies solely on miscoverage indicators (actual feedback), whether the true label falls within the interval at each time step, while overlooking the empirical prediction threshold (estimated feedback) that is derived from the oracle conformal method. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Dual-feedback Conformal Inference (DDCI), which incorporates a dual-feedback mechanism consisting of actual feedback and estimated feedback. The former drives the primary adjustment of the intervals based on true observations, while the latter dampens excessive expansions or contractions by leveraging empirical thresholds from conformal inference during updates. By balancing these two signals, DDCI achieves more stable and narrower prediction intervals in sequential settings while maintaining near-nominal coverage in practice.
core_methodology: Dynamic Dual-feedback Conformal Inference (DDCI) incorporates both actual feedback (based on miscoverage indicators) and estimated feedback (empirical prediction threshold from conformal inference) to adjust prediction intervals adaptively in time series forecasting. This dual-feedback mechanism aims to balance stability and accuracy, maintaining near-nominal coverage while producing narrower intervals.
data_sources: Primarily applicable to sequential data prone to temporal dependence and distributional changes, suitable for financial time series data such as asset prices, volatility, or other market indicators.
alpha_potential: DDCI can enhance trading strategies by providing more reliable and stable uncertainty quantification for time series forecasts, which is crucial for risk management and adaptive trading models. It may improve the robustness of algorithmic trading strategies by reducing overreaction to volatile market conditions and avoiding excessive adjustments in prediction thresholds.
title_cn: 时间序列预测中的动态双反馈保形推断
summary_cn: 本文提出的动态双反馈保形推断（DDCI）方法，通过结合实际反馈和估计反馈，优化了时间序列预测中的不确定性量化。对于量化交易而言，该方法可提供更稳定、更准确的预测区间，有助于优化风险管理和自适应交易策略，减少市场波动对预测模型的过度影响。

title: Bayesian Neural Networks via Dirichlet Process Priors on the Data-Generating Distribution for Randomized Value Functions in Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) offer a principled framework for quantifying epistemic uncertainty. However, standard weight-space priors yield complex, high-dimensional neural network posteriors that are computationally prohibitive to sample from, and popular approximate inference schemes often fail to capture epistemic uncertainty effectively---a failure mode particularly acute in reinforcement learning (RL) \citep{osband2018randomized}. To resolve this challenge, we introduce a new class of BNNs that quantify uncertainty by placing Bayesian nonparametric Dirichlet Process (DP) priors directly on the underlying data-generating distribution rather than on network parameters. Building on this foundation, we develop DP-DQN, a reinforcement learning algorithm that leverages DP-BNNs to maintain posterior distributions over value functions and perform efficient Thompson sampling. By grounding randomized value functions in Bayesian nonparametrics, DP-DQN unifies data-driven posterior reweighting (via the Bayesian Bootstrap) with generative prior hypotheses injected directly through the DP base measure, enabling decisive ``deep exploration'' with a single neural network without the overhead of multi-network ensembles.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) with Dirichlet Process (DP) priors on the data-generating distribution, focusing on quantifying epistemic uncertainty in reinforcement learning. Specifically, it presents DP-DQN, an algorithm that leverages DP-BNNs for maintaining posterior distributions over value functions and performing efficient Thompson sampling.
data_sources: The methodology is data-agnostic but can be applied to any sequential decision-making problem, including financial time-series data or order book data in trading contexts.
alpha_potential: The approach offers potential for capturing epistemic uncertainty in trading strategies, which can lead to more robust decision-making in volatile markets. The ability to perform deep exploration with a single neural network could reduce computational overhead compared to ensemble methods, potentially uncovering novel trading signals.
title_cn: 基于数据生成分布狄利克雷过程先验的贝叶斯神经网络在深度强化学习随机值函数中的应用
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种新颖的贝叶斯神经网络框架，通过数据生成分布的狄利克雷过程先验来量化认知不确定性，并开发了DP-DQN强化学习算法。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于价值函数后验分布建模，通过高效的Thompson采样实现更稳健的市场策略决策，特别适用于高波动性市场环境。

title: Dissecting the Impact of Model Misspecification in Data-driven Optimization
summary: Data-driven optimization aims to translate a machine learning model into decision-making by optimizing decisions on estimated costs. Such a pipeline can be conducted by fitting a distributional model which is then plugged into the target optimization problem. While this fitting can utilize traditional methods such as maximum likelihood, a more recent approach uses estimation-optimization integration that minimizes decision error instead of estimation error. Although intuitive, the statistical benefit of the latter approach is not well understood yet is important to guide the prescriptive usage of machine learning. In this paper, we dissect the performance comparisons between these approaches in terms of the amount of model misspecification. In particular, we show how the integrated approach offers a ``universal double benefit'' on the top two dominating terms of regret when the underlying model is misspecified, while the traditional approach can be advantageous when the model is nearly well-specified. Our comparison is powered by finite-sample tail regret bounds that are derived via new higher-order expansions of regrets and the leveraging of a recent Berry-Esseen theorem.
core_methodology: Comparison of traditional maximum likelihood estimation versus integrated estimation-optimization approaches for decision-making under model misspecification, with finite-sample regret analysis
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to any data-driven optimization problem (could be applied to portfolio optimization signals or trading rule parameter estimation)
alpha_potential: Addresses the critical issue of model error propagation in trading systems - could improve robustness of signal generation or portfolio construction frameworks that rely on ML estimates
title_cn: 剖析模型误设在数据驱动优化中的影响
summary_cn: 本研究对比了传统最大似然估计与集成估计-优化方法在模型误设情况下的表现，对量化交易中的信号生成和组合优化具有重要启示。当模型存在误设时，集成方法可显著降低决策误差，这对依赖于机器学习模型的交易系统尤其有价值。

title: Robust Residual Correction via Selective Deployment for Time Series Forecasting
summary: Post-hoc residual correction can reduce forecasting error, but always-on updates often fail to generalize: when residual signals are weak or noisy, expressive correctors can overfit and even increase the overall forecasting errors. We introduce CRC, a robust residual correction framework that couples a hybrid corrector with a validation-calibrated selective deployment rule. CRC proposes corrections via a conservative ridge "floor" plus conditional nonlinear refinement, but deploys them only when held-out evidence indicates net error reduction over a frozen baseline forecaster. CRC treats when to revise a forecast as a validation-calibrated deployment decision, not only how to fit residuals. Across standard long-sequence benchmarks and multiple backbones, CRC improves horizon-averaged MSE and MAE in most dataset-backbone pairs, with particularly large gains on complex datasets (e.g., over 20% relative MSE reduction on Traffic). We additionally report the non-degradation rate (NDR) as a stability diagnostic of harmful updates and ablate the validation-calibrated "firewall" that stabilizes MSE gains.
core_methodology: A robust residual correction framework (CRC) that combines a conservative ridge-based approach with conditional nonlinear refinement, using a validation-calibrated deployment rule to selectively apply corrections only when they are likely to reduce forecasting errors.
data_sources: Standard long-sequence benchmarks, including complex datasets like Traffic, though specific financial datasets are not mentioned, the methodology is adaptable to financial time series.
alpha_potential: The selective deployment of corrections can improve forecasting accuracy in financial time series, particularly in volatile or noisy market conditions where overfitting is a risk. This could enhance trading signals or risk management models by reducing forecast errors without degrading performance during stable periods.
title_cn: 时间序列预测中通过选择性部署实现的稳健残差校正
summary_cn: CRC框架通过验证校准的选择性部署规则，结合保守的岭回归基础和条件非线性细化，仅在残差校正能降低预测误差时应用，避免过拟合。该方法可提升金融时间序列预测的准确性，尤其适用于市场波动大或噪声多的环境，为交易信号优化和风险管理提供潜在优势。

title: StartLux-Decision: AutoThink Decision Models with Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Deliberative Decisions
summary: We introduce StartLux-Decision, decision models from 0.8B to 27B parameters that combine efficient single-pass prediction with adaptive, confidence-guided reasoning. The Instant models use bidirectional attention in full-attention layers to improve decision accuracy while keeping single-pass inference. The AutoThink models invoke explicit reasoning for uncertain decisions and answer confident cases directly. A three-stage training pipeline establishes shared decision capabilities, specializes the two variants, and equips AutoThink with reasoning through reasoning supervision and reinforcement learning. We introduce Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Deliberative Decisions (RLCD$^2$), which uses a frozen model and proper scoring rules to reward improvements in decision probability quality and applies a soft penalty to overlong reasoning traces. RLCD$^2$ raises the share of reasoning traces that terminate within the generation limit by up to 48 percentage points and cuts average reasoning length by up to 65%, while largely preserving decision accuracy. On the public subset of Decision Index 0.3, the Instant models outperform the strongest evaluated comparable-scale open-weight decision models by 7.4-16.9 points, and the 27B AutoThink model reaches 73.4. We also introduce DecisionPivot, a programmatically verifiable benchmark of computational decisions built from contrast pairs that differ in a single answer-changing detail. On DecisionPivot, AutoThink outperforms its Instant counterparts by 11.5-18.4 points in pair accuracy and leads among evaluated systems. The models can be run using frameworks such as vLLM and MLX, with quantized versions available to reduce memory usage.Inference code and links to model weights are available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/Startlux-Decision .
core_methodology: StartLux-Decision combines efficient single-pass prediction with adaptive, confidence-guided reasoning. The Instant models use bidirectional attention for single-pass inference, while AutoThink models invoke explicit reasoning for uncertain decisions. Training involves a three-stage pipeline for shared decision capabilities, specialization, and reasoning reinforcement learning (RLCD$^2$).
data_sources: Public subset of Decision Index 0.3 and DecisionPivot benchmark, which includes contrast pairs differing in answer-changing details.
alpha_potential: Potential to enhance decision accuracy in trading by dynamically balancing speed and deliberation, especially for uncertain market conditions where adaptive reasoning could identify mispricings or optimize execution strategies.
title_cn: StartLux-Decision：基于强化学习的校准思考决策模型
summary_cn: StartLux-Decision提出了一种结合高效单次预测与自适应置信引导推理的决策模型，通过三阶段训练流程和强化学习优化决策质量。在交易中，该技术可动态平衡决策速度与深度，特别适用于不确定市场条件下的定价误差识别或执行策略优化，展现量化交易的实用潜力。

title: Dynamic portfolio selection under range value-at-risk with logarithmic returns
summary: This paper studies continuous-time portfolio selection under Range Value-at-Risk (RVaR), with both portfolio performance and risk evaluated in terms of logarithmic returns. We formulate a mean--RVaR problem in a continuous-time financial market and reduce the dynamic optimization to a static quantile problem. Using quantile representation, Lagrangian optimization, and convexification, we characterize the optimal terminal wealth through the convex envelope of an RVaR-specific transformed weighting function. The RVaR-specific convex envelope exhibits two distinct geometric configurations. Under Scenario~1, the terminal wealth has a VaR-type structure: the minimum-RVaR payoff is digital-option-like, whereas for $0<\lambda<1$ it consists of two growth-optimal regions separated by a constant-payoff region. Under Scenario~2, the convex envelope is determined either by a supporting line connecting an interior contact point to the endpoint or by a common supporting line with two interior contact points, leading to a richer multi-region payoff structure. We further show that the RVaR solutions reduce to their VaR and Expected Shortfall (ES) counterparts as $\beta\downarrow\alpha$ and $\alpha=0$, respectively. Under constant investment opportunities, we also derive closed-form wealth processes and replicating portfolio strategies. Numerical results show that the effects of $(\alpha,\beta,\lambda)$ on risky-asset exposure are nonlinear and generally non-monotone. In particular, when $\alpha>0$, pure minimum-RVaR optimization may assign zero terminal wealth in sufficiently bad states because the extreme quantile region $[0,\alpha)$ is excluded from the RVaR criterion. These results clarify how interval-based quantile risk control shapes state-dependent portfolio payoffs and connects RVaR with its VaR and ES limiting cases.
core_methodology: The paper employs continuous-time portfolio optimization techniques using Range Value-at-Risk (RVaR) with logarithmic returns. It uses quantile representation, Lagrangian optimization, and convexification methods to characterize optimal terminal wealth. The methodology involves dynamic optimization reduced to static quantile problems with specific geometric configurations for payoff structures.
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to generic continuous-time financial markets; implementation would require historical price data and return series for calibration.
alpha_potential: The approach offers a sophisticated risk-management framework that goes beyond traditional VaR/ES by controlling risk over return intervals. This could capture tail-dependent behaviors and state-contingent portfolio payoffs that are overlooked by standard risk measures, potentially identifying regime-specific alpha opportunities.
title_cn: 基于对数收益范围风险价值的动态投资组合选择
summary_cn: 本文研究了在连续时间金融市场上基于范围风险价值(RVaR)的投资组合优化问题，通过对数收益衡量绩效与风险。通过静态分位数重构和凸化方法，揭示了两种不同的最优终端财富几何结构。该方法改进了传统VaR/ES的风险控制，可生成状态依赖的资产配置策略，对于开发具有尾部风险保护的量化策略具有实用价值。

title: Expert-Guided Rubrics as Dense Reward Signals for Reinforcement Learning in Non-Verifiable Domains
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in non-verifiable domains such as financial services, where they must interpret user intent, rewrite queries, and retrieve information under domain-specific constraints. Although reinforcement learning (RL) can train such agents from the consequences of their actions, recent successes largely rely on verifiable tasks with automatically computed binary rewards. In non-verifiable retrieval tasks, assessing query quality requires scarce subject-matter expert (SME) judgment that is inherently graded rather than binary. With Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), sparse rewards yield no useful learning signal when all sampled outputs within a group receive the same outcome, causing optimization to stall. We introduce a method that converts a small, fixed investment of SME judgment into a dense reward and combines it with retrieval-based metrics to form a hybrid, GRPO-compatible training signal. Experiments show improvements of up to 6\% in Recall@3 and 6.7\% in MRR@3 compared with sparse-reward baselines.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a method combining expert judgment with retrieval-based metrics to create dense rewards for reinforcement learning in non-verifiable domains, specifically using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
data_sources: Subject-matter expert (SME) judgments and retrieval-based metrics in non-verifiable domains like financial services.
alpha_potential: Potential application in improving automated financial service agents through better query interpretation and information retrieval, which could indirectly enhance quantitative trading strategies relying on such services.
title_cn: 专家引导的规则作为非可验证领域中强化学习的密集奖励信号
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种方法，将专家判断与检索指标结合，为非可验证领域（如金融服务）的强化学习提供密集奖励信号。这种方法可优化金融领域中的自动代理性能，间接提升依赖此类服务的量化交易策略。实验显示在检索任务中性能提升达6%。

title: Teaching AI Agent to Play Poker Strategically Through Preference Optimization
summary: A poker agent can make a legal move and still make a strategically poor one. We ask whether compact AI agents can exhibit strategic behavior under hidden information and whether preference optimization can improve beyond static and zero-shot policies. We first evaluate a static baseline and three frozen language models: SmallThinker, Qwen3, and Gemma-3 whose performance varies substantially between exact-game and six-player evaluation. We therefore propose Strategic Preference Optimization with KL-anchored Equilibrium (SPOKE), combining teacher-relative value penalties, policy anchoring, risk constraints, and structured rationale supervision, and compare it with SFT, DPO, GRPO, and GSPO. Across three runs of a SmallThinker-4B-A0.6B policy, SPOKE achieves the lowest mean exploitability in Kuhn (0.213) and Leduc (1.081) and the highest six-max top-1 agreement (0.775), while maintaining teacher KL comparable to SFT (0.522 vs 0.523). These results provide preliminary evidence that strategic preference optimization can improve strategic quality while preserving teacher-consistent behavior.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Strategic Preference Optimization with KL-anchored Equilibrium (SPOKE), which combines teacher-relative value penalties, policy anchoring, risk constraints, and structured rationale supervision to improve AI agents' strategic decision-making under hidden information in poker. It compares SPOKE with SFT, DPO, GRPO, and GSPO.
data_sources: The evaluation is conducted on simulated poker games (Kuhn and Leduc) using AI models like SmallThinker, Qwen3, and Gemma-3, focusing on strategic behavior and exploitability metrics.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to trading scenarios with incomplete information or strategic decision-making, such as market making or adversarial trading environments. The focus on risk constraints and structured rationale supervision may also be relevant for portfolio optimization.
title_cn: 通过偏好优化教授AI代理策略性玩扑克
summary_cn: 本文提出的SPOKE方法通过结合相对价值惩罚、策略锚定和风险约束，改进了AI在隐藏信息环境下的策略决策。这一方法在模拟扑克游戏中表现出色，未来可应用于交易策略中的不完全信息决策，如做市或对抗性交易场景。

title: RGH-GNN : Risk-Gated Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network for Financial Fraud Detection
summary: Credit card fraud is a significant problem for financial institutions, resulting in substantial monetary loss each year. Fraud patterns and methods are continuously evolving, with fraudulent transactions often disguised to resemble legitimate activity. Real world transaction data for fraud detection is severely affected by class imbalance making it harder to detect these transactions. Fraudulent transactions are rarely isolated. Accounts, devices, and other common attributes are often shared across fraudulent activity, revealing relational patterns that individual transaction features alone cannot capture. Graph-based approaches model these relationships explicitly. However, standard graph neural networks aggregate neighbourhood information uniformly, which can dilute the already scarce signal carried by fraudulent transactions and limit detection of camouflaged fraud. This work presents RGH-GNN, a heterogeneous graph neural network that addresses this limitation by incorporating transaction-level risk scores, generated by a supervised LightGBM classifier as edge weights. It is used to guide message passing through a learnable risk-gated aggregation mechanism. It ensures that high-risk transactions contribute more strongly to learned representations rather than being diluted by uniform neighbourhood aggregation. RGH-GNN is evaluated on the IEEE-CIS fraud detection dataset against standard graph neural network models that are trained on the same heterogeneous graph. RGH-GNN outperforms all baselines across every evaluation metric, with an AUC-ROC score of 0.914. This demonstrates that incorporating engineered risk signals into graph-based message passing substantially improves fraud detection performance.
core_methodology: Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network (GNN) with risk-gated aggregation mechanism using transaction-level risk scores as edge weights
data_sources: IEEE-CIS fraud detection dataset (credit card transaction data)
alpha_potential: Potential to detect fraud patterns through relational analysis between transactions and accounts, which could be adapted for detecting manipulation patterns in trading data
title_cn: RGH-GNN：用于金融欺诈检测的风险门控异构图神经网络
summary_cn: 该研究提出了基于风险门控机制异构图神经网络(RGH-GNN)的欺诈检测方法，通过将交易风险评分纳入图神经网络的消息传递过程，显著提高了欺诈交易检测性能(AUC-ROC 0.914)。这种方法可潜在应用于识别交易市场中的操纵行为模式。

title: Fixed-Size Active Statistical Inference
summary: Variance reduction techniques improve the efficiency of drawing conclusions from data. Recent proposals for variance-reduction use two complementary techniques to reduce variance: incorporating machine learning predictions into estimators and weighted sampling. A popular weighted sampling algorithm is Poisson Sampling (PS), which independently flips a biased coin at each unit and includes all heads in the sample. A fundamental flaw with PS is that it has a random sample size, which presents practical challenges and introduces variance into the estimator. We show that a fixed-size alternative, known in survey sampling as Conditional Poisson Sampling (CPS), is a drop-in replacement for PS on general multivariate Z-estimation problems, which include convex M-estimation considered in prior work. Notably, we show that the asymptotic variance of CPS is no worse than that of PS, and can be substantially better in realistic scenarios where predictions are imperfect. We illustrate these advantages on both synthetic and real datasets, and release a Python package implementing CPS. In light of our contributions, there is no need to suffer a variable sample size.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Conditional Poisson Sampling (CPS) as a fixed-size alternative to Poisson Sampling (PS) for variance reduction in statistical inference. It demonstrates that CPS can be used in general multivariate Z-estimation problems, including convex M-estimation, and shows that CPS has better or comparable asymptotic variance to PS.
data_sources: The paper uses both synthetic and real datasets, though the specific nature of the real datasets is not detailed in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be applied to improve the efficiency of statistical estimators in quantitative finance, such as in portfolio optimization or risk assessment, by reducing variance in sampling-based approaches. However, the direct application to trading strategies is not immediately clear.
title_cn: 固定大小的主动统计推断
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种名为条件泊松采样（CPS）的固定大小采样方法，用于替代传统的随机大小泊松采样（PS），以在统计推断中降低方差。该方法在多种Z估计问题中表现优异，特别适用于不完美预测的现实场景。在量化金融中，CPS可能有助于提高投资组合优化和风险评估中的统计估计效率，但直接应用于交易策略仍需进一步研究。

title: AnchorRM: Parallel Intra-Batch State Reconstruction with Anchor-Based Residual Memory for Temporal Graph Neural Networks
summary: Memory-based temporal graph neural networks (TGN) rely on recurrent node memories to capture evolving interaction histories. However, temporal mini-batching introduces a trade-off between computational efficiency and temporal fidelity: when a node appears multiple times within the same batch, later interactions are evaluated using stale pre-batch memory because the intermediate memory updates have not yet been committed. This problem becomes more severe as temporal batch size increases. To overcome this challenge, we propose AnchorRM, an anchor-based residual memory mechanism that reconstructs event-specific intra-batch node states without executing sequential recurrent updates. AnchorRM treats the last committed node memory at the beginning of each batch as a pre-batch fixed anchor and uses causally preceding same-batch interactions to infer the missing state evolution relative to that anchor. The learned residual then calibrates the anchor to reconstruct an event-specific node memory for each interaction. Because each event-specific residual is predicted directly from the fixed anchor and its causal history, reconstructed states do not depend on previously reconstructed states and can therefore be computed in parallel within the batch while preserving temporal causality. Experiments across four temporal graph datasets and three memory-based backbones demonstrate that AnchorRM achieves an average 6.16x training speedup (up to 10.05x) and 28.67x batch scaling (up to 40x). These results demonstrate that AnchorRM substantially improves the scalability and training efficiency of memory-based temporal graph learning while maintaining competitive predictive performance.
core_methodology: The paper introduces AnchorRM, an anchor-based residual memory mechanism for temporal graph neural networks (TGN) that reconstructs event-specific intra-batch node states without requiring sequential recurrent updates. It uses causally preceding same-batch interactions to infer missing state evolution relative to a fixed anchor, enabling parallel computation while preserving temporal causality.
data_sources: The methodology was tested across four temporal graph datasets, though specific financial datasets were not mentioned. The approach is general and could be adapted to financial temporal graphs such as transaction networks or order book dynamics.
alpha_potential: AnchorRM's ability to efficiently capture evolving interaction histories in temporal graphs could be applied to model market microstructure dynamics, such as order flow or limit order book evolution, potentially uncovering short-term predictive signals. The parallel processing capability is particularly relevant for high-frequency trading scenarios where latency is critical.
title_cn: AnchorRM：基于锚点残差内存的并行批内状态重建用于时序图神经网络
summary_cn: AnchorRM提出了一种创新的残差内存机制，通过固定锚点和因果历史推断实现时序图节点状态的并行重建。这一方法可显著提升时序图学习效率（10倍加速），在保持预测性能的同时支持40倍批量扩展。在量化交易中，该技术有望用于高效建模市场微观结构动态（如订单流时序关系），为高频交易策略提供低延迟的时序模式识别能力。

title: Two Is Enough: Binary Classification Priors Suffice for Multi-Class In-Context Tabular Prediction
summary: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) pretrain a transformer on large-scale synthetic priors so that a single forward pass yields zero-shot tabular prediction. TabICLv2 samples the class count of its classification prior during pretraining, and the prevailing configuration caps it at ten. We report a counter-intuitive result: setting this cap directly to two---making every pretrained classification task binary---still yields weights that perform zero-shot K-way classification 2. On the 38 TabArena classification datasets (200 bootstrap rounds, anchored at default RF = 1000), the binary two-stage recipe reaches 1590.1 Elo, above the official default at 1568.0 (+22.1), above TabPFN-v2.6 (1577.1) and RealTabPFN-v2.5 (1521.6). A production-scale validation on 60 real-world credit-scoring institutions independently confirms the direction: the same checkpoint improves test AUC on 44 of 60 institutions (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.0007 for AUC, p = 0.0002 for KS) at +1.5 inference cost. Mechanistically, classification in TabICLv2 is carried not by a fixed-cardinality output head but by an in-context comparison operator matching query-row embeddings against class-conditional embeddings, so the cardinality of the output space is set by the labels present in the context, not by the label space seen during pretraining. This makes a binary prior structurally cheaper to generate and cache than a ten-class prior, demotes "number of classes" from an architectural constraint to a tunable hyperparameter, and points to a class-count-agnostic regime of TFM pretraining.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a novel approach to tabular foundation models (TFMs) by demonstrating that binary classification priors can effectively perform multi-class classification through in-context learning, leveraging transformer architectures and embedding comparisons.
data_sources: The methodology is validated on 38 TabArena classification datasets and further tested on 60 real-world credit-scoring institutions, indicating a focus on structured financial data.
alpha_potential: The technique showcases potential for improving performance in classification tasks relevant to credit scoring and financial decision-making, with demonstrated improvements in AUC and KS metrics, which could translate to better predictive modeling for risk assessment.
title_cn: 二进制分类先验足够进行上下文表格预测中的多类分类
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种新颖的表格基础模型方法，表明仅使用二进制分类先验即可通过上下文学习进行多类分类，提升了信用评分等金融领域的预测性能。其核心是嵌入比较而非固定输出头的架构变化，适用于结构化财务数据。该方法在38个数据集和60家信用机构上验证了性能提升（AUC增加），显示出在风险预测模型中的应用潜力。

title: From POMDP Theory to Deep RL with Particle Filters
summary: Model-based reinforcement learning in partially observable environments requires inferring hidden states, learning latent dynamics, and planning under the resulting belief. Practical algorithms often solve one aspect of the above pipeline while relying on approximations for the others that are often poorly understood, while existing POMDP theory typically analyzes computationally inefficient theoretical algorithms far from modern deep RL practice. To fill this gap, we propose a practical end-to-end algorithm that approximately solves the hidden state filtering problem via sequential Monte Carlo (SMC), updates a latent dynamics model online, and performs approximate online planning for $d$ steps before bootstrapping leaves with a state-value critic (a QMDP approximation). We analyze each approximation and prove an end-to-end regret bound decomposing the error into model estimation error, particle filter error, Monte Carlo rollout error, and a structural bias term induced by the QMDP approximation controllable by the planning depth that we further analyze in various special cases. The resulting guarantee makes explicit how statistical sample size, particle budget, rollout budget, and planning depth affect performance. We instantiate our algorithm in an MPC-based deep RL framework, demonstrating its practicality on a variety of environments. On a POMDP that satisfies our assumptions, each term of the bound decays at its predicted rate. Our results provide a practical and theoretically grounded route for bridging theory and practice within online decision-making in POMDPs.
core_methodology: The paper presents an end-to-end algorithm combining sequential Monte Carlo (particle filtering) with model-based reinforcement learning for partially observable environments. It integrates hidden state inference, online latent dynamics learning, and approximate planning with QMDP approximation.
data_sources: Not explicitly financial data, but methodology is applicable to any time-series data with hidden states (e.g., market microstructure, latent factors)
alpha_potential: Potentially useful for (1) learning hidden market regimes, (2) modeling latent price dynamics in imperfectly observable markets, (3) developing adaptive execution algorithms under partial observability
title_cn: 从POMDP理论到基于粒子滤波的深度强化学习
summary_cn: 该论文提出的结合序贯蒙特卡洛(粒子滤波)与强化学习的混合算法,可用于金融市场的隐状态建模(如潜在市场机制转换)及部分可观测环境下的优化决策。虽需领域适配,但其理论框架为开发适应市场不确定性的量化策略提供了新思路。

title: Pairwise Learning Increases Data Efficiency in Deep Neural Networks
summary: Deep neural networks often fail at small-sample regression, collapsing to low-variance predictions that miss individual differences. Here, we introduce a pairwise comparison framework that reframes regression as aggregated relative rankings. This method improves data efficiency across model architectures and dataset sizes. On the UTKFace dataset (23k images), pairwise learning generates over one billion training comparisons without additional supervision. The paired ranking allows a lightweight ResNet10 trained from scratch on home hardware to achieve a 3.64-year MAE-surpassing previous models, including those with large-scale pretraining. For classification into categories, pairwise supervision consistently outperforms an otherwise identical 10-way crossentropy model on STL10 with 500-2000 labeled examples, improving accuracy by up to 5.2%. Overall, pairwise supervision enhances data efficiency and enables strong regression and classification performance when labeled data are limited, particularly in clinical settings.
core_methodology: Pairwise comparison framework reframing regression as aggregated relative rankings to improve data efficiency in deep neural networks
data_sources: UTKFace dataset (23k images) for baseline validation (not financial data)
alpha_potential: Potential to extract more signal from limited labeled financial datasets (e.g., alternative data annotations, earnings surprise rankings) by learning relative relationships instead of absolute values
title_cn: 成对学习提升深度神经网络的数据效率
summary_cn: 该论文提出的成对比较框架通过将回归问题重构为相对排名聚合，显著提高了小样本场景下的模型效能。在量化交易中，此方法可优化有限标注财务数据（如分析师评级排序、事件冲击强度排序）的利用效率，提升因子挖掘和事件驱动的信号质量。

title: From Complex Histories to Simple Predictors: Predictive Dimension in Dynamic Graph Learning
summary: Existing continuous-time graph learning methods rely heavily on complex neural architectures to encode ever-expanding interaction histories. However, the future conditional distribution induced by complex histories can often be characterized by a low-dimensional predictive state manifold, implying that only a few predictive degrees of freedom are essential for future interactions. We therefore argue that continuous-time graph learning should identify low-dimensional states sufficient for future prediction rather than reconstruct the full history. To make this perspective measurable, we define and independently estimate the intrinsic predictive dimension, which quantifies the effective predictive degrees of freedom required by a given task. Specifically, we remove the history-independent marginal from the history-conditioned future distribution, decompose the resulting predictive residual operator, and estimate the minimum effective rank needed to preserve the predictive power of the full history. Experiments across datasets show that model performance saturation is largely determined by the intrinsic predictive dimension. Based on this finding, we propose PreDyG, a lightweight model whose capacity is matched to the intrinsic predictive dimension. PreDyG achieves superior predictive performance with only 0.07\% of the parameters of a representative complex baseline.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the concept of intrinsic predictive dimension to identify low-dimensional states sufficient for future prediction in dynamic graphs, rather than reconstructing full interaction histories. It proposes PreDyG, a lightweight model whose capacity matches this intrinsic predictive dimension.
data_sources: The paper uses dynamic graph datasets, which could be analogous to financial networks such as trade flows, transaction networks, or interbank lending networks.
alpha_potential: The methodology could help in identifying simplified yet effective predictive states in financial networks, potentially improving predictions of market movements or systemic risks by focusing on the most predictive features rather than complex historical data.
title_cn: 从复杂历史到简单预测器：动态图学习中的预测维度
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种基于动态图的预测方法，通过识别低维预测状态而非复杂历史数据，提高预测效率。在金融网络中应用时，该方法可简化预测模型，专注于关键预测特征，可能提升市场走势或系统性风险的预测准确性。

title: A Semi-Analytical Inference Framework for Structural Causal Models
summary: Structural Causal Models (SCMs) provide a principled framework for observational, interventional, and counterfactual reasoning, all of which rely on probabilistic inference. Existing frameworks either transform SCMs into alternative tractable representations or rely on approximate inference with expressive generative models. We instead perform inference using a message passing scheme directly on the SCM by representing structural mechanisms and probability densities in a common finite-dimensional function space. Forward propagation combines a numerical realization of the Law of the Unconscious Statistician, while propagated densities are recovered by spline projection from LOTUS moments. The same representation naturally yields backward message passing for conditioning, providing a unified framework for causal inference. Using tensor-product B-spline bases, the resulting algorithm expresses inference through numerical quadrature and linear algebra without explicitly constructing conditional distributions. Experiments on randomly generated continuous SCMs demonstrate accurate approximation of Monte Carlo reference solutions and systematic improvement with increasing basis resolution.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a semi-analytical inference framework for Structural Causal Models (SCMs) using message passing schemes and tensor-product B-spline bases. It focuses on causal inference through numerical quadrature and linear algebra.
data_sources: The paper uses randomly generated continuous SCMs for experiments, which are synthetic data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for causal inference in financial markets, potentially identifying causal relationships in market data for improved trading strategies.
title_cn: 结构因果模型的半解析推理框架
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种结构因果模型（SCM）的半解析推理框架，通过消息传递和张量积B样条基进行推理。虽然在实验中使用了合成数据，但该框架可应用于金融市场的因果分析，帮助识别潜在的市场因果关系，为交易策略开发提供新的视角。

title: Causal Discovery for Linear Models with Latent Confounding via Multi-domain Identifiable Representation Learning
summary: Causal discovery with latent confounding is particularly challenging, but a common setting in real-world data. In this work, we focus on linear causal models with latent confounding, represented by acyclic directed mixed graphs (ADMGs). Existing methods that fully identify ADMGs typically assume non-Gaussianity or graphical constraints, such as bow-freeness. In contrast, we propose Linear ADMG Learning (LinADMG), a framework for learning ADMGs for linear causal models through identifiable representation learning. Rather than relying on non-Gaussianity or bow-freeness, LinADMG leverages multi-domain settings to identify the noise variables. We show that the identifiability of the noise variables is sufficient for recovering all direct causal relations, and that, under an additional latent-confounding no-cancellation condition, LinADMG can identify the whole ADMG. We implement LinADMG with four identifiable representation learning approaches from the literature and validate the methods on simulated and semisynthetic datasets.
core_methodology: A framework for learning acyclic directed mixed graphs (ADMGs) in linear causal models with latent confounding through identifiable representation learning, leveraging multi-domain settings to identify noise variables.
data_sources: Simulated and semisynthetic datasets (no real financial data mentioned in the abstract).
alpha_potential: Potential for identifying causal relations in financial markets which could help in constructing robust trading signals by understanding direct causal effects beyond correlation. However, requires adaptation to financial time series.
title_cn: 通过多域可识别表示学习发现具有潜在混淆的线性模型的因果关系
summary_cn: 该论文提出了LinADMG框架，通过多域环境和可识别表示学习来解决线性因果模型中潜在混淆的问题。虽然主要基于模拟数据，但其识别直接因果关系的能力可能有助于金融市场中超越相关性的信号构建，需要进一步适应金融时间序列数据。

title: Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment for LLM Reasoning over Temporal Knowledge Graphs
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) often struggle with temporally grounded reasoning because their static parametric memory is misaligned with the dynamic evolution of real-world knowledge. Although RAG and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) provide practical ways to enhance LLMs, they remain insufficient for temporal reasoning. Existing retrieval methods typically prioritize semantic relevance while overlooking temporal validity, event order, and evolutionary dependencies, resulting in evidence that is relevant in isolation but temporally fragmented. Meanwhile, conventional PEFT methods usually employ fixed and input-agnostic low-rank updates, making it difficult to capture time-dependent entity semantics and relation drift. To address these limitations, we propose Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment (TEPCA), a framework for LLM reasoning over TKGs. TEPCA aligns LLM reasoning with temporal knowledge at both the evidence and parameter levels. At the evidence level, it introduces time-constrained Dynamic Relevance-Guided Path (DRGP) pruning to preserve globally coherent temporal paths, together with Mutual-Information (MI)-based pruning to retain query-informative local facts under temporal constraints. At the parameter level, it integrates Dynamic-Gated LoRA (DG-LoRA), a timestamp-conditioned low-rank adaptation mechanism that dynamically modulates the effective adaptation subspace according to temporal context. This design enables LLMs to better capture fine-grained entity evolution and time-dependent relation semantics while preserving parameter efficiency. Experimental results on two TKG benchmarks demonstrate that TEPCA achieves state-of-the-art performance. Additional evaluations of DG-LoRA on eight commonsense QA datasets further verify its general input-adaptive capacity, scalability across LLM backbones, and interpretability.
core_methodology: Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment (TEPCA) framework combining time-constrained Dynamic Relevance-Guided Path pruning and Dynamic-Gated LoRA for temporal reasoning in LLMs
data_sources: Temporal Knowledge Graphs (TKGs) and eight commonsense QA datasets
alpha_potential: Potential to improve temporal reasoning in financial event analysis, earnings prediction, and market sentiment tracking by better capturing time-dependent relations and entity evolution
title_cn: 面向时序知识图谱的LLM推理中时间证据-参数协同对齐方法
summary_cn: TEPCA框架通过动态时间约束路径剪枝和时间门控LoRA机制，显著提升LLM在时序知识推理中的表现。在量化交易中，该方法可优化财报事件分析、产业链关系演化跟踪等时序敏感任务，通过精确捕捉实体语义的时间漂移来获取市场动态信号。

title: ChartEvo: Self-Evolving Agent Harnesses for Long-Tail Chart Reasoning
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have substantially advanced chart understanding and reasoning, yet their performance remains highly uneven across chart types. While modern MLLMs perform well on common charts, their accuracy drops sharply on long-tail charts with diverse visual structures and reasoning requirements. Tool-augmented agents can improve complex chart reasoning by introducing specialized visual capabilities, but manually engineering strategies and tools for the heterogeneous and evolving long tail is difficult to scale. We introduce \textbf{ChartEvo}, a recursive self-improvement framework that enables chart agents to adapt to underperforming chart types through experience-driven harness-level self-improvement. ChartEvo jointly evolves reusable chart-specific Skills and executable Tools, while learning reusable local tool-call chains to compose evolved capabilities and control the inference overhead of tool-augmented reasoning. On long-tail charts from ChartBench and ChartX, ChartEvo improves accuracy over its base MLLM, Qwen3.7-Plus, by \textbf{45.6\%} and \textbf{32.5\%}, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of recursive self-improvement for long-tail chart adaptation.
core_methodology: Recursive self-improvement framework for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to enhance performance on long-tail chart types through experience-driven evolution of chart-specific Skills and Tools, with optimization for inference overhead in tool-augmented reasoning.
data_sources: Long-tail charts from ChartBench and ChartX datasets (specific financial data sources not explicitly mentioned in the abstract).
alpha_potential: Potential to improve the analysis of complex or uncommon chart patterns that current MLLMs struggle with, which could be applied to identifying unique trading signals or anomalies in financial markets with non-standard visual representations.
title_cn: ChartEvo：自进化智能体研究框架实现长尾图表推理
summary_cn: ChartEvo通过递归自改进框架，优化多模态大语言模型针对长尾图表的理解和推理能力。该方法可应用于金融市场的特殊图表模式识别，为交易策略提供更准确的市场信号分析工具。

title: Rewards for Budget-Aware Multi-Turn Agents That Adapt to Arbitrary Test-Time Constraints
summary: Large language model agents are often given an inference budget and asked to maximise success within it. A multi-turn agent has to allocate this budget across many environment interactions. An external harness can enforce the budget, but it remains unclear whether the agent itself can learn when and how much to spend. We ask whether agents can learn this allocation across dynamically specified budgets and which rewards best teach this behaviour. We adapt existing length penalties to budget constraints spanning multiple resource types, introduce new reward formulations, and compare eleven objectives in a shared training pipeline. We train Qwen3.5 models at 4B and 9B on AppWorld with budgets over tokens, API calls, and environment steps, and on the BabyAI gridworld with turn budgets. We train a separate policy for each environment and resource type, with each policy trained across budget values. Training with rewards that penalise overspending substantially improves within-budget success and natural compliance over untrained models and over training on task success alone, with agents learning to adapt their resource use to stated budgets and task difficulty. These gains extend to unseen budgets and, zero-shot, to a shifted task distribution and a new benchmark. Reward objectives trade off success within budget and natural compliance. A sigmoid penalty for overspending most often achieves the highest within-budget success at an individual budget, while a fixed negative reward for overspending generally yields the strongest natural compliance. Combining penalties for overspend frequency and magnitude gives the smallest average gap to the best method at each budget. Overall, we show that a single agent can learn to allocate resources across turns and adapt its behaviour to user-specified budgets using budget feedback without external budget-allocation controllers.
core_methodology: The paper explores reinforcement learning techniques for budget-aware multi-turn agents, specifically focusing on how agents can learn to allocate resources (tokens, API calls, environment steps) efficiently across multiple turns under dynamically specified budgets. It evaluates various reward formulations to optimize within-budget success and natural compliance.
data_sources: Experiments are conducted in simulated environments (AppWorld and BabyAI gridworld) with budgets over tokens, API calls, and environment steps, rather than real-world financial data.
alpha_potential: While not directly tested on financial data, the methodology could potentially be adapted to optimize resource allocation in algorithmic trading, such as managing API call budgets for real-time market data or computational resource allocation in high-frequency trading systems.
title_cn: 适应任意测试时间约束的预算感知多轮智能体奖励机制
summary_cn: 本文研究多轮智能体在动态预算约束下的资源分配问题，通过强化学习优化预算内任务成功率和自然合规性。该方法可潜在应用于量化交易中的API调用管理、高频交易计算资源分配等场景，提升系统效率。

title: Geometry-Agnostic Data-Driven Discovery of Extreme Scenarios
summary: We introduce a two-stage data-driven neural framework for discovering dynamically admissible extreme scenarios. Rather than assuming prior knowledge of the governing equations, the first stage infers the effective dynamical constraints directly from observational data. When the underlying physical system possesses suitable symmetries, the learned dynamics can be represented in a geometry-agnostic form, independent of any fixed grid, coordinate system, dimensionality, and intrinsic curvature. In the second stage, a physics-informed neural-search uses this learned dynamics to uncover rare, high-impact coherent structures that may not have appeared in the original observations. We demonstrate this framework through representative examples of increasing dimensionality and geometric complexity. Starting from a traditionally learned Duffing dynamics, we find a homoclinic pulse as a plausible localized extreme scenario. Next, since the same equation also appears in the stationary nonlinear Schrodinger system, with the coordinate interpreted as space instead of time, this pulse becomes a standing soliton. We then retrain the first stage using a geometry-agnostic neural representation, enabling the learned dynamics to be lifted to higher-dimensional space to obtain higher-dimensional solitary profile, known as Townes soliton. Finally, with a Liouville system, we demonstrate that dynamics learned from data on a (1+1)-dimensional Lorentzian quasi-manifold can be transferred to a (2+0)-dimensional Euclidean manifold to identify an instanton. Our approach can be applied to other coherent spatiotemporal structures, including kinks, rogue waves, compactons, peakons, and potentially even singularities, with applications in risk analysis, nonlinear forecasting, and anomaly detection.
core_methodology: Two-stage neural framework: 1) Infers dynamical constraints from observational data without prior knowledge of governing equations 2) Uses physics-informed neural-search to uncover rare, high-impact coherent structures. The approach is geometry-agnostic, handling systems with various symmetries.
data_sources: General observational data for dynamical systems (not market-specific in the paper but adaptable to financial time series)
alpha_potential: Potential for identifying rare market regimes, extreme events, and nonlinear patterns that conventional models miss. Could be adapted for tail risk forecasting and anomaly detection in markets.
title_cn: 几何无关的数据驱动极端情景发现方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种两阶段神经网络框架，可发现动态可容许的极端情景。第一阶段从观测数据推断有效动态约束，第二阶段通过物理信息神经搜索揭示罕见的高影响力结构。该方法能够辨识传统模型可能遗漏的非线性模式，应用于金融市场时可改进尾部风险预测和异常检测。

title: Model- and Layer-Level Closed-Loop Forecasting with SSM-Based Spiking Neural Networks
